items.note: Amtsblatt Nr. 24/2025, 'bereitgestellt am 11.12.2025', printed on p. 463 (contents list confirms), Stadt Neustadt am Rübenberge: Rat resolved on 19.06.2025; par. 1 sets 1,20 EUR for one hour, 2,40 EUR for 2,5 hours, up to half an hour free; par. 3 takes effect on the 14th day after the day of promulgation and repeals the Parkgebührenordnung of 24.09.2024. All claims match. Note: the 2025/062 council paper expected entry into force around 1 Aug 2025, but the gazette printing is dated 11 Dec 2025, so the ordinance only took effect in late December 2025.

Same gazette page, par. 2: e-plate vehicles (EmoG, FZV marking) pay no fee while charging at a charging post when using a parking disc, for a maximum of 2,5 hours; the exemption ends with the expiry of the EmoG at the end of 31.12.2026; the Rathaustiefgarage is excluded. All claims match.

Beschlussvorlage 2025/062 dated 27.05.2025: after half a year of charging, the Schützenplatz is 'so gut wie überhaupt nicht angenommen'; drivers move to surrounding residential streets, the Leinepark event-centre lot and the west side of the station (free); the free spaces on Suttorfer Straße and at Leinepark are during the day 'an der Grenze der Aufnahmefähigkeit'. The 2024 charge came from the 5.9.2024 budget-stabilisation decision. Title and number match. It is a proposal paper; the draft's wording is neutral and correct.

City press release of 3 April 2025 (Yannik Behme): the mayor wants to make Schützenplatz parking free again and will propose a change to the fee ordinance; electric cars should be exempt from the fee while charging at public charging posts, with a parking disc. The paper states that charging started in October 2024 and that the intended effect failed to appear. It is worded as proposals, as in the draft; the June 2025 decision is confirmed by the gazette (item 0).

City press release of 8 Oct 2024 (written before the date): machines at Schützenplatz and Kleiner Brink (Mardorf) to be switched on Thursday 17 Oct 2024; 1,20 EUR per hour, 2,40 EUR for the 2,5-hour maximum; 'Brötchentaste' half hour free kept; 3 EUR day ticket at Schützenplatz; new machines at Leinstraße and Wallhof; added note that old machines were reprogrammed on 18 Dec 2024. The page is a pre-event announcement, but the April 2025 press release (item 3) and paper 2025/062 independently confirm that charging at Schützenplatz had been in force since October 2024 (half a year of operation), so the past-tense wording is acceptable. Kleiner Brink charging itself is confirmed also by the live parking page (item 5).

Live undated city page read in full: about 750 'bewirtschaftete Parkplätze' in the centre; 30 minutes free with the Kurzparktaste; 1,20 EUR per hour; 2,5 hours maximum for 2,40 EUR; charges Mon-Fri 9-17 and Sat 9-13, around the town hall Mon-Fri 7-17 and Sat 9-13; town-hall garage open daily 6-21, 'sonntags geschlossen' (the page contradicts itself; the draft repeats both without comment, which is acceptable). Dating to 2026-10 / read on 21 October 2026 is as the brief requires. The page text is as the draft says; the 750 figure is a current city statement (compare the ~400 in January 2021, item 9, which is a different count date).

Same live parking page: ten numbered car parks P1-P10 with 50, 70, 80 (town-hall garage), 69, 80 (Schützenplatz, 'kostenlos'), 18, 60, 23, 24 and 110 (Tiefgarage Neustadttor, 'kostenpflichtig') spaces, so 10 lots from 18 to 110; Parkgarage Am Wallgraben 270 spaces, 'kostenpflichtig'. Text: Neustadttor garage 'wird privat bewirtschaftet'; Wallgraben garage 'im Eigentum der Wirtschaftsbetriebe Neustadt', permanent permits can be applied for. All claims match. Note that the page says 'Eigentum' (owner) for Wallgraben, not that Wirtschaftsbetriebe operates it; the draft says 'owned', which is right.

The notice exists at the bottom of the live parking page: 'Kein kostenloses Parken mit E-Kennzeichen! Wichtig! Fahrer von elektrisch betriebenen Fahrzeugen müssen ebenfalls eine Parkgebühr bezahlen, wenn sie ihr Auto auf den bewirtschafteten Parkplätzen in der Neustädter Innenstadt oder auf dem Parkplatz Kleiner Brink in Mardorf parken wollen.' The draft says this 'conflicts' with the ordinance. That is too strong: the ordinance (item 1) only exempts e-plate cars while they are charging at a charging post (max 2,5 h, disc), so the notice may refer to cars that are not charging or may simply be outdated. The page itself carries no date. Low confidence is right.
items.corrected_text: The city's parking page (read on 21 October 2026) carries a notice headed 'Kein kostenloses Parken mit E-Kennzeichen' saying electric-car drivers must also pay on the managed lots in the centre and at Kleiner Brink. The June 2025 ordinance (printed December 2025) exempts e-plate cars only while charging at a charging post, up to 2.5 hours with a parking disc, until 31 December 2026, so the notice may be outdated or may refer to cars that are not charging; the page is undated and the city does not explain the difference.

items.note: Press release of 13 Sep 2024 is written before the event: the garage 'wird am Montag, 16. September, für die Öffentlichkeit freigegeben'. All numbers match (54 public spaces plus 6 spaces for e-vehicles with charging; free for now; one-hour maximum with parking disc; Mon-Fri 7-19 'bis auf Weiteres'; paid management planned 'mittelfristig', machines expected 'voraussichtlich noch in diesem Jahr'). The page cannot show that it actually opened on that date (a later paper, 2025/062, only shows the garage exists with 12 charging boxes, a different EV count from the 6 EV spaces in this notice). Per brief the opening must be worded as announced, not as completed fact.
items.corrected_text: On 13 September 2024 the city announced that the underground garage below the new town hall would open to the public on Monday 16 September 2024, with 54 public spaces and 6 spaces for electric vehicles with a charging option. Parking would be free at first with a one-hour limit (parking disc), open Monday to Friday 7-19 until further notice, with paid management planned for later (machines expected that year). A later council paper (2025/062) mentions 12 charging boxes in the garage, which the city has not reconciled with the 6 spaces named here.

items.note: Press release of 28 Jan 2021, written before the start: 'ab dem kommenden Montag, 1. Februar' payment by app, call or SMS is possible; the page says 'eingeführt' but is an announcement. Details match: Ideenstadtwerke, initiative 'smartparking', seven providers (EasyPark, Park now, Mobilet, Yellowbrick/flowbird, paybyphone, Parkster, Parco), rund 400 bewirtschaftete Parkplätze in der Innenstadt, Parkgarage Am Wallgraben excluded because of the barrier system, tariff 1 Euro for up to 2,5 hours. The private lot between ZOB and Wunstorfer Straße was also excluded. Wording must be 'announced to start'.
items.corrected_text: On 28 January 2021 the city announced that mobile-phone parking payment (app, call or SMS) would be available from Monday 1 February 2021 on about 400 managed parking spaces in the town centre, through the smartparking initiative with seven app providers and in cooperation with the Ideenstadtwerke. The Am Wallgraben garage was excluded because of its barrier system, as was a private lot between the bus station and Wunstorfer Straße. The tariff at that time was 1 euro for up to 2.5 hours and phone users pay a provider service fee.

items.note: Press release of 8 Oct 2021, written before the closure: 'Ab Sonntag, 24. Oktober, steht das Areal zwischen der Sparkasse und dem Kaufhaus H&M nicht mehr als Parkfläche zur Verfügung'; Wallgraben garage 'in der Regel gut 80 Parktaschen frei' on normal working days, 'an Markttagen (freitags) bei Weitem nicht ausgelastet'; fee in the garage 'wird ... halbiert' to one euro for two hours during the town-hall construction. Numbers match, but the draft states the closure and the fee halving as completed facts. The page also says 70 more bays were expected behind the station from January 2022 (not in the draft).
items.corrected_text: On 8 October 2021 the city announced that the large car park between the Sparkasse and H&M would close from Sunday 24 October 2021 for the town-hall construction. It said the Wallgraben garage usually had well over 80 free spaces on normal working days and was far from full on Friday market days, and announced that the garage fee would be halved to 1 euro for two hours for the duration of the works.

items.note: bahnhof.de page (plain HTTP 200, no bot wall) lists three 'Offene Parkmöglichkeit' entries 'Neustadt a Rübenberge P+R', all at An der Eisenbahn, with 73, 55 and 75 Stellplätze insgesamt, Mo-So incl. holidays 00:00-00:00. No tariff and no statement whether the lots are separate; refers to parkenambahnhof.de. The draft's wording matches. The page is undated and live, so dating to 2026-10 / read on 21 October 2026 is correct. Medium confidence is appropriate for an undated live listing.

Beschlussvorlage 2019/182 dated 19.08.2019 (Rat date 19.09.2019, no vote recorded in the document). List 5 and text match except one item: the draft says 'rebuilding the Wallgraben/Rundeel parking deck', but the list says 'Sanierung oder Neubau der Parkpalette Wallgraben/Rundeel' (renovation or rebuilding). Other items: 'Errichtung Parkhaus West für Park & Ride-Nutzung und weitere öffentl. Parkplätze', 'Tiefgarage und Außenparkplätze am neuen Rathaus', 'Neubau Parkplatz am Schloss/VHS', charging stations at public lots, 'Überprüfung, wo und wieviel Parkgebühren erhoben werden', and 'seit langer Zeit einen großen Bedarf an P+R-Parkplätzen westlich des Bahnhofes'. These are goals for feasibility studies, not decided projects (the draft says the vote is not shown, which is right).
items.corrected_text: A 2019 council proposal (Beschlussvorlage 2019/182, dated 19 August 2019) on mobility goals to 2030 for the town centre listed, as goals to be studied, a P+R parking garage west of the station with further public spaces, an underground garage and surface parking at the new town hall, a new car park at the castle/VHS site, renovating or rebuilding the Wallgraben/Rundeel parking deck, charging stations at public car parks and a review of where and how much parking fee is charged. It noted a long-standing large demand for P+R spaces west of the station and parking lost to building projects; the document does not show how the council voted.

items.note: Informationsvorlage 2020/077 of 04.05.2020: the draft Nahverkehrsplan 2020 of the Region Hannover (draft decided by the Regionsversammlung on 3 March 2020, consultation running, city comments due 1 Oct 2020) rates the P+R expansion need as high priority at the Kernstadt station, medium in Eilvese, low in Hagen and Poggenhagen. Measure list: 'Ausbau P+R am Bahnhof in der Kernstadt'. Worded correctly as a draft, not a decision.

Consultant slides (Büro Zacharias, 'Termin 10.12.2024 - Verkehrliche Grundlagen und Maßnahmenplanung', 23 pages, all read): page 21 'Maßnahmenplanung/Empfehlungen' lists Parken Schützenplatz 'mit neuer Brücke für Fuß + Rad anbinden, Shuttle in Kernstadt', 'Erweiterung Parken Am Walle ggf. durch Parkpalette', 'Optimierung Parkgarage Am Wallgraben', 'Befestigung P+R, Anbindung Innenstadt'; page 10 goal 'Attraktive Stellplatzanlagen am Rande der Kernstadt (Verkehrsvermeidung)'. Worded as recommendations; correct. Slides only, no text of decisions.

Beschlussvorlage 2022/270 of 24.11.2022 (Marktstraße Süd): private car park of 24 spaces opposite the new town hall excluded from city ownership; development step 2 for 2024 'ca. 24 provisorischen oberirdischen Parkplätzen nahe am Rathausneubau'; citizens' forum feedback included the wish for above-ground parking close to shops. Matches. It is a proposal (decision pending in committees), and the draft words it as 'planned', which is acceptable.

ecomento.de article dated 14.05.2026 (trade-press rewrite of an E.ON press release): E.ON put four new Deutschlandnetz fast-charging sites into operation including Neustadt am Rübenberge; all installed stations up to 400 kW; Neustadt park has three roofs with 27 kWp PV and six charging stations with twelve charging points near the B 6 at Famila, Rudolf-Diesel-Ring 30. The exact opening day is not given; 'May 2026' is the article date. Secondary source for a fact that E.ON or Deutschlandnetz itself would confirm; medium confidence is correct.

Beteiligungsbericht Stand 30.06.2026: Wirtschaftsbetriebe Neustadt am Rübenberge GmbH is '100%' in the city's ownership; its purpose is that it 'betreibt unmittelbar Anlagen und Einrichtungen des ruhenden Verkehrs, der Energiegewinnung, die Vermarktung von Energie', property, and spa/pool operations and street lighting. The draft is wrong that the report 'does not give parking figures': page 10 has a segment table 'Sparte Parken' with a result of 56.578 EUR in 2024 and 10.326 EUR in 2023 (financial result, not capacity or usage). Also the report does not say the company runs 'the town's' parking, only that it operates parking facilities.
items.corrected_text: Wirtschaftsbetriebe Neustadt am Rübenberge GmbH, wholly owned by the city, directly operates facilities for stationary traffic (parking) along with energy generation and sales, property and swimming-pool and street-lighting activities (Beteiligungsbericht, status 30 June 2026). The report gives no space counts or usage data for parking, but its segment table shows a parking result of 56,578 euros for 2024 and 10,326 euros for 2023.

corrected_summary: Neustadt am Rübenberge sets paid parking by city ordinance. A new fee ordinance was decided by the council on 19 June 2025 and printed in the Region Hannover gazette on 11 December 2025, taking effect on the 14th day after promulgation: 1.20 euros per hour or 2.40 euros for 2.5 hours, with the first half hour free. The city's parking page (read on 21 October 2026) says about 750 managed spaces in the centre are charged Monday to Friday 9-17 and Saturday 9-13; a 2021 city statement counted about 400 managed spaces. Charging started on the Schützenplatz and the Kleiner Brink lot in Mardorf on 17 October 2024, and the Schützenplatz is now listed as free after a council paper said it was barely used and drivers moved to free streets and the west side of the station. The city lists ten numbered car parks of 18 to 110 spaces, the Wallgraben garage (270 spaces, owned by Wirtschaftsbetriebe Neustadt), the privately run Neustadttor garage (110) and the town-hall garage, which the city announced would open in September 2024 (54 public plus 6 EV spaces at that announcement; the city page now says 80). Cars with an e-plate park free for up to 2.5 hours while charging at a charging post until the Electromobility Act expires at the end of 2026, but the city page still carries a notice that e-car drivers must pay, which may be outdated. Phone parking was announced for 1 February 2021. A fast-charging park by E.ON was reported opened in May 2026. DB lists three P+R entries on An der Eisenbahn with 73, 55 and 75 spaces; council papers since 2019 and the 2020 draft regional transport plan mention P+R demand at the station, and a December 2024 consultant slide set recommends paving the P+R, but no expansion project was found and no usage figures exist.
